transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (CTO, Nebula), Lena (ML Eng), Marta (Infra)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery for migration off OpenAI. Focus on compatibility with current stack (vLLM/TGI), eval parity concerns, and Dedicated/VPC requirements. Agreed to run benchmarks and exchange security docs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, I'm Jordan with Redwood, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros - I'm the AE, Priya is our solutions engineer who'll run through the technical bits.
[00:12] Samir: Hey Jordan, Samir here, CTO at Nebula. We run a few prod services that rely on OpenAI today but looking to move to dedicated infra for cost and data controls.
[00:20] Lena: Hi! Lena, ML eng - I own model infra and evaluation. We also use vLLM for local benchmarking and TGI in some pipelines.
[00:30] Marta: Marta, infra - interested in VPC and KMS integration and the network topology.
[00:37] Jordan: Great. Priya, do you want to kick off with a high level on how Redwood Dedicated fits?
[00:42] Priya: Sure. Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, VPC peering, private control plane, and KMS integrations. We support model variants and automatic fallback policies. The idea is you get the same API as hosted but within your tenancy.
[01:05] Lena: Two quick things up front - eval parity. When we ran Mistral and Llama-2 locally with vLLM we saw slight quality diffs versus OpenAI outputs. How do you guarantee parity?
[01:20] Priya: Good question. We typically run a side-by-side eval. There are three levers: model artifact compatibility (weights/tokenizer), runtime differences (kv cache, attention kernels), and tokenization variances. We recommend bringing your eval prompt sets; we run them on our runtime and compare metrics. For many customers differences are within noise but we do see edge cases.
[01:45] Samir: Can you run the exact same vLLM config? We use vLLM with some custom kernel flags and sequence chunking.
[01:55] Priya: We can run with vLLM-style configs where possible. Our runtime supports similar hyperparameters - batch sizes, kv cache strategies - but some low-level kernel flags may map differently. We'll try to match them and note any differences in perf and outputs.
[02:15] Jordan: Important for us to understand your latency and cost targets - Samir, what are you aiming for?
[02:22] Samir: For our chat product we need p95 latency ~300ms on 2k token context and cost target is roughly 60% of our current OpenAI spend. We're seeing big token volume so unit economics matter.
[02:35] Priya: 300ms p95 on 2k is tight but achievable with the right GPU type and batching profile. Our recommendations will depend on model size and quantization. Which models are you running?
[02:48] Lena: Mostly Llama-2-13B and a few finetuned 7B variants. We also have a small fleet of Claude equivalents for some tasks.
[02:58] Marta: On infra side, network egress and peering - we need private peering into our VPC and support for customer-managed KMS. SOC2 docs too.
[03:10] Priya: We support VPC peering, private control plane and bring-your-own-KMS (HSM integrations available for enterprise). SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 are available in our security pack - I'll share the docs.
[03:25] Samir: Great. A lot of our risk is around regressions after migration. How do we do safe rollout?
[03:33] Jordan: Our rollouts allow canaries and automatic fallback to hosted model variants, you can pin routes and do gradual traffic shifting. We also expose per-route dashboards for model quality metrics.
[03:45] Lena: Do you support function calling and structured outputs? We rely heavily on deterministic JSON outputs from the model.
[03:53] Priya: Yes, function/tool calling and structured output helpers are supported. We also have eval hooks that tie regressions to prompt sets so you can alert on quality drift.
[04:06] Samir: About compatibility - we use TGI for some reproducible transforms, and vLLM for fast local testing. Is exporting/tarballing model weights enough to run on Redwood?
[04:18] Priya: Usually yes, if the model is in a supported format (HF, ggml, safetensors). We have a model onboarding guide. For TGI-specific artifacts we may need to convert tokenizer metadata; we can help with that.
[04:35] Lena: We've seen tokenization differences on huggingface converters - sometimes spaces are merged differently, causing output shifts.
[04:43] Priya: Yup, that's common. We'll run tokenization parity tests as part of the onboarding benchmark.
[04:55] [00:05:00] (background noise) Speaker 1: sorry -
[05:10] Jordan: No worries. Quick commercial question: do you need reserved capacity or would a hybrid with hosted fallback make sense?
[05:19] Samir: Initially reserved - we want predictable costs. If benchmarks show parity and perf we may stay reserved.
[05:27] Marta: We also need compliance controls; if we go on-prem we need air-gapped options. Any enterprise on-prem package?
[05:35] Priya: We offer a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with a private control plane and on-prem package for regulated workloads. On-prem has additional disk encryption and isolated networking.
[05:47] Lena: For evals, can we run our existing automated regression suite? It expects APIs similar to OpenAI.
[05:56] Priya: Our API is OpenAI-compatible for generation/embedding endpoints and includes streaming. For more advanced features we have compatible wrappers; we'll work with you to minimize changes.
[06:10] Samir: Cost - do you have an optimizer or recommendations for batching/caching to reduce token spend?
[06:18] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Optimize gives batching/caching suggestions and quantization profiles. We can propose a config to hit your 60% cost target.
[06:28] Lena: How do you handle KV cache across shards? We had cache flush issues in earlier infra that increased latency.
[06:36] Priya: Our runtime manages KV cache and supports shard-local caches with smart routing to keep warm prefixes pinned. We can share tracing of cache hit rates during benchmarks.
[06:47] Marta: Network: what ports and DNS changes are needed for peering? We need a network diagram.
[06:55] Jordan: We'll share a network topology doc and the specific ACL/peering steps.
[07:04] Lena: A technical question - do you run quantized int8 kernels? We use 4-bit quantization in prod for some models.
[07:14] Priya: We support quantization-friendly execution paths including int8 and int4 for certain model architectures. We'll need to validate quality impact on your finetuned models.
[07:26] Samir: Can Priya run a quick compatibility smoke test with one of our 7B finetuned checkpoints?
[07:33] Priya: Yes, if you can share a checkpoint or S3 access. We can try to reproduce locally and on Dedicated.
[07:41] Samir: We'll share a token-limited S3 link.
[07:45] Jordan: Let's talk timelines - are you aiming to migrate before year-end?
[07:51] Samir: Preferably before EOY, but realistically Q1. We want a pilot in the next 3-6 weeks.
[07:58] Jordan: That works. We'll prioritize the benchmark to prove perf and parity.
[08:05] Lena: One more thing: inference throughput. We have bursty traffic with large context in mornings - need autoscale + burst.
[08:14] Priya: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity. We'll propose an autoscale policy and reserve a burst buffer for your peak windows.
[08:23] Marta: For KMS, can we use our Azure Key Vault?
[08:28] Priya: Yes, we have KMS integrations across AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault; we can walk through the IAM permissions.
[08:36] Samir: Regarding security reviews, our legal wants the SOC2 report and a data flow diagram.
[08:43] Jordan: We'll send SOC2 Type II, ISO certs, and a data flow doc.
[08:49] Lena: When you run benchmarks, can you provide both latency percentiles and qualitative eval examples (diffs)? We want to see both numbers and sample outputs.
[08:59] Priya: Absolutely - we'll provide a performance sheet (p50/p95/p99), cost per 1k tokens, and a side-by-side output diff for a selected prompt set.
[09:09] Samir: What about model security - can you lock down model uploads and RBAC for team roles?
[09:16] Priya: Yes, RBAC for model access and model-level permissions are supported. Audit logs are available for uploads and inference calls.
[09:24] Jordan: Will you be using any private models with PHI?
[09:29] Samir: Some redacted patient notes in a search product - so sensitive, yes. That's why KMS and on-prem options are important.
[09:36] Priya: For PHI we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated in a VPC with customer-managed KMS and enhanced audit retention.
[09:44] Marta: Cost question again - licensing for dedicated is commit-based?
[09:49] Jordan: Dedicated has monthly/annual reserve contracts. We can provide a few tiers based on GPU type and capacity.
[09:58] Lena: A nit - does Redwood's tokenizer cause occasional truncation differences at token boundaries? We saw this in one Open-source runtime where stop tokens behaved oddly.
[10:10] Priya: We have configurable stop token handling; we'll validate your stop token behavior during tests.
[10:17] Samir: Ok, next steps? I want concrete deliverables.
[10:21] Jordan: We'll do: 1) Jordan sends sizing/pricing, 2) Priya runs compatibility test after you share S3 checkpoint, 3) Lena shares eval prompts and traffic sample, 4) schedule infra deep dive next week.
[10:36] Marta: Sounds good. Also send the network peering doc and port list.
[10:41] Jordan: Yep.
[10:45] Lena: One small ask - we have an internal spreadsheet mapping current OpenAI API usage patterns (streaming vs non-streaming). Will you accept that as input for sizing?
[10:52] Jordan: Yes, that will help. Send that to the workspace and we'll use it in the cost model.
[10:58] Samir: If benchmarks show a 10-15% quality regression but cost is 50% lower, what do you recommend?
[11:06] Priya: We usually propose a hybrid: use Dedicated for high-volume non-critical paths and keep hosted for critical flows, or try quantization/finetune/LLM-ops to close the gap. Also you can A/B test per route with rollouts.
[11:22] Lena: Do you support in-line finetuning or adapter-based low-cost finetune?
[11:28] Priya: We support adapter workflows and fine-tune pipelines; for Dedicated we can run fine-tune jobs and host the resulting model. We'll review data governance for fine-tuning PHI.
[11:40] Jordan: Any blockers on your side for sharing the checkpoint and prompts?
[11:45] Samir: We'll confirm access with legal and send a limited S3 token.
[11:50] Priya: Thanks. I'll kick off the smoke test once we have access.
[11:54] Jordan: Alright, we'll wrap with a short recap.
[11:58] Jordan: Recap: Jordan to send pricing and network docs, Priya to run compatibility smoke test, Lena to share eval prompt sets and traffic sample, and schedule infra deep dive for next week.
[12:11] Marta: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[12:14] Samir: Thank you.
[12:16] Priya: Thanks - we'll follow up in the workspace and post the benchmark plan.
[12:20] (meeting ends)
